initializeResponse.instructions:
This server controls DeepSeek Harness (DSH) sessions through the DSH ACP profile.
Typical flow: dsh_list_sessions -> dsh_create_session or dsh_resume_session -> dsh_send_message -> dsh_close_session.
Always pass an explicit session_id; the bridge never assumes "the most recent session".
A resumed session continues the persisted conversation but does NOT replay prior transcript content.
DSH tool permission requests are denied unless permission_policy="allow_once" is passed explicitly.
DSH internal thoughts are not returned unless the bridge operator enabled DSH_CODEX_INCLUDE_THOUGHTS.

tools.name: dsh_list_sessions
tools.title: List DSH sessions
tools.description: List persisted, resumable DSH root sessions from the ACP session/list method (newest first). Optional cwd filter must be an absolute path inside the allowed directories. Returns only sessionId/cwd/title/updatedAt summaries. WARNING: sessions held by the desktop app are also listed (ACP cannot see cross-process activity); visibility does not mean the session is free.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory to filter by (realpath validated).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous nextCursor field.

tools.name: dsh_create_session
tools.title: Create a DSH session
tools.description: Create a fresh persistent DSH session via ACP session/new. cwd must be absolute, inside the configured allowlist, and is realpath-canonicalised before use. model / reasoning_effort are only accepted when explicitly allowlisted by the bridge.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory for the new session.

model.description: Optional model id; must be allowlisted (DSH_CODEX_ALLOWED_MODELS).

reasoning_effort.description: Optional reasoning effort; must be allowlisted (DSH_CODEX_ALLOWED_REASONING_EFFORTS).

profile.description: Optional DSH profile; must equal the bridge profile.

tools.name: dsh_resume_session
tools.title: Resume a DSH session
tools.description: Restore a persisted inactive DSH session via ACP session/resume, validating canonical cwd and session ownership first. Resume only restores a persisted inactive session and continues it; it does not replay prior transcript messages. WARNING: DSH ACP cannot see sessions held by another process (the desktop app), so session/list also lists sessions the desktop may still be running. Resuming is NOT read-only: it activates the session and writes to the same persisted log, which can conflict with the desktop. Requires acknowledge_released=true, and switching desktop tabs does not count as releasing.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory; must match the session canonical cwd.

acknowledge_released.description: Must be true. Confirms the session is not in use by the desktop app (closed there, not merely a background tab).

permission_policy.description: Default permission policy recorded for later prompts.

tools.name: dsh_send_message
tools.title: Send a message to a DSH session
tools.description: Send one user text message to an existing session via ACP session/prompt and wait for the turn to settle. Exactly one prompt may be in flight per session. Returns the assistant text, a tool-call summary and usage. DSH internal thoughts (agent_thought_chunk) are NOT returned unless the operator set DSH_CODEX_INCLUDE_THOUGHTS. Permission requests made by DSH tools are DENIED unless permission_policy is explicitly "allow_once"; they are never auto-approved.

session_id.description: Explicit session id (never defaulted to "most recent").

permission_policy.description: How to answer DSH tool permission requests for this turn.

timeout_ms.description: Prompt settlement timeout; capped by the bridge prompt timeout.

tools.name: dsh_cancel_session
tools.title: Cancel a DSH session run
tools.description: Ask the ACP session/cancel method to stop the work of exactly one session. The in-flight prompt settles with stopReason "cancelled"; other sessions are untouched.

tools.name: dsh_close_session
tools.title: Close a DSH session
tools.description: Close exactly one session via ACP session/close. This cancels in-flight work, drains updates, flushes persistence, and releases the session run scope. Persisted history is retained and can be resumed later. Requires confirm=true. Closing is NOT read-only and is NOT a safe way to inspect a session; it will cancel that session's in-flight work.

confirm.description: Must be true: closing cancels in-flight work and releases run resources (history is kept; it is not read-only).
